Title: AI in our cyber work: colleague showcase
Why: Generic courses cannot establish actual bank adoption.
Agenda: Three worked cases and cross-domain discussion; distinguish production, restricted pilots and horizon ideas.
Evidence: Explain one own-domain and one adjacent-domain case, limits and changed human work.
Prerequisites: Verified case owners, sanitised evidence and approved status labels.

Title: Approved platform, architecture and safe use
Why: Teach the actual model, agent, connector, permission and data boundaries.
Agenda: Architecture walkthrough, data classification choices, permissions and a stop/escalation demonstration.
Evidence: Trace a request across model, tools and data; choose safe inputs and identify the accountable owner.
Prerequisites: Approved architecture and data/access guidance; simulation if learner access is unavailable.

Title: Limitations, AI-enabled threats and knowledge check
Why: Use bank examples for current limitations, spoofing and AI-enabled attacks.
Agenda: Short threat briefing, planted false outputs and knowledge check with feedback.
Evidence: Recognise unsupported output and suspicious content, explain uncertainty and choose verification/escalation.
Prerequisites: Current sanitised cases, answer key and support route.

Title: Responsible AI-assisted work case
Why: A generic app project is insufficient evidence of bank work.
Agenda: 30m task/model/context setup; 60m supported task with reset and verification; 30m review and handover.
Evidence: Produce a sourced work result, correct a planted error, manage session context and retain responsibility.
Prerequisites: Approved tool or realistic simulator, safe task data, answer criteria.

Title: Supervise, intervene and recover
Why: Supervision needs observed behaviour in the approved environment.
Agenda: Define autonomy and escalation; inspect traces; inject a tool/output failure; stop, revoke and recover.
Evidence: Correctly delegate, monitor, intervene, recover and record the human decision.
Prerequisites: Seeded failure traces, validated recovery path, scoped permissions.

Title: Create, own and retire a shared Skill
Why: TR-191 improves generic Skills teaching; bank ownership, connector vetting, review and deprecation still require local practice.
Agenda: Create a focused Skill; attach tests and failure modes; peer-review permissions; assign monthly review and retirement rules.
Evidence: Submit a tested Skill, named owner, provenance, connector decision, change triggers and deprecation procedure.
Prerequisites: Agreed template, library workflow, approved connector list and notification route.

Title: Domain benchmarks and release checks
Why: Use representative bank tasks and known faults rather than generic model success.
Agenda: Build small normal/adversarial test sets; compare a baseline and a change; interpret failures and release checks.
Evidence: Retain expected answers, failure classes, acceptance criteria and a release/reject decision.
Prerequisites: Sanitised tasks, reviewed answer key and evaluation harness.

Title: Observed supervision sign-off
Why: Course completion does not demonstrate workplace performance.
Agenda: Integrated blind task, failure injection, evidence review and feedback.
Evidence: Complete the task with safe intervention; any critical control failure requires remediation and reassessment.
Prerequisites: Calibrated assessors and rubric; operational permission is separately approved.

Title: Build, evaluate and deploy a scoped agent
Why: Integrate build and evaluation decisions in a prepared bank scaffold.
Agenda: Define task and alternatives; build workflow; compare cost/latency; use human-labelled tests; aggregate errors; plan hosting, monitoring and rollback.
Evidence: Demonstrate versioned agent, reproducible evaluation, human-calibrated judgements, error analysis and release/stop decision.
Prerequisites: Approved scaffold, synthetic data, current APIs, security/identity experts available; prerequisites confirmed.

Title: Independent builder challenge
Why: Validate decisions and failure handling separately from coached construction.
Agenda: Unseen change and failure challenge; review evidence, monitoring and rollback; assess or return for remediation.
Evidence: Defend build/buy/model choice, detect drift and demonstrate a safe correction or withdrawal.
Prerequisites: Blind cases, calibrated rubric and approved testing environment.

Title: Risk case and independent challenge
Why: Apply bank governance and risk controls to a real responsibility.
Agenda: 4h risk case covering ownership, tiering, evidence, third parties and lifecycle; 2h independent challenge.
Evidence: Decision record, control mapping, accountability, residual-risk decision and escalation.
Prerequisites: Current bank policy, approved case and authorised risk decision-makers.

Title: Workflow and adoption decision studio
Why: Use bank strategy and work evidence to make accountable adoption decisions.
Agenda: Compare current and proposed workflow, humans and controls; choose vendor/tool criteria and measures.
Evidence: Document baseline, proposed operating model, accountable owners and adopt/pilot/reject decision.
Prerequisites: Verified use case, tool evidence and decision authority.

Title: Quarterly evidence and adoption forums
Why: Keep adoption accountable as tools and work change.
Agenda: Four 1h forums, one per quarter; review benefits, risks, workforce effects, feedback and stop/scale choices.
Evidence: Four logged decisions with measures, owners, action dates and follow-up.
Prerequisites: Baseline metrics and reliable feedback; Q1 establishes the baseline.
